claim.quote: We find the total cross section falls toward the threshold less steeply than expected from two-gluon exchange models.

key_value_text.quote: The differential cross section $d\sigma /dt$ has an exponential slope of $1.67 \pm 0.39$ GeV$^{-2}$ at $10.7$ GeV average energy.
key_value_text.value: exponential slope of dσ/dt of 1.67 ± 0.39 GeV^-2 at 10.7 GeV average energy

name: GlueX near-threshold J/psi photoproduction
notes: Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 123, 072001 (2019); dated by the arXiv v1 submission.

summary.plain: GlueX measured how often a photon striking a proton produces a J/ψ particle, from 11.8 GeV all the way down to the production threshold. It saw no sign of the LHCb pentaquark candidates in this channel and set upper limits.
summary.technical: First measurement of the γp→J/ψp cross section from Eγ=11.8 GeV down to threshold (8.2 GeV) with the tagged photon beam; the total cross section falls toward threshold less steeply than two-gluon exchange models expect; dσ/dt slope 1.67±0.39 GeV^-2 at 10.7 GeV; no evidence for LHCb Pc+ states in the s-channel, with model-dependent upper limits on their branching fractions.

title: First measurement of near-threshold J/ψ exclusive photoproduction off the proton
why_it_matters: Near-threshold J/ψ production is sensitive to the gluonic structure of the proton and is the channel in which s-channel pentaquark resonances could appear.
